articles.title: Magic: The Gathering’s Newest Legendary Artifact Destroys Whole Universes (and Your Creatures)
articles.summary: Magic: The Gathering’s next set is the world-bending Reality Fracture, which centers around an alternate universe with twisted mirror versions of many the game’s characters.
body: The first card is a key object in Reality Fracture: The Echoverse Fulcrum. This Mythic Rare legendary artifact is meant to merge universes together, but its functional effect is a board wipe with a little bit of card selection attached.

Colorless cards have had plenty of conditional board wipes like this before, but to my eyes, the low initial mana cost and immediate benefit of drawing and then discarding a card could make this one more broadly useful in a format like Commander. Five mana to activate its ability and only at sorcery speed are both real drawbacks, but that’s easier to stomach when you’ve already gotten something (admittedly minor) out of it.

The other card we are revealing depicts the final moments of Reality Fracture’s hero-turned-villain, Jace. Vraska’s Final Mercy is a Rare sorcery that can either be a removal spell or effectively draw you two cards as it either strikes down or builds up Jace himself.
points: Magic: The Gathering’s next set is the world-bending Reality Fracture, which centers around an alternate universe with twisted mirror versions of many the game’s characters.

articles.title: GTA 6 Developer Is Fighting Drones And Hackers To Keep The Game’s Secrets Safe
articles.summary: As the studio behind one of the most highly anticipated games of all time, GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games has divulged more details on how it keeps its secrets. As part of a hearing, which began yesterday at the Glasgow Employment Tribunal--in which Rockstar Games has been accused of unlawfully…
body: "Guarding the secrets of the unique gameplay and design are akin to Apple protecting the iPhone or Coke protecting its formula," Rockstar said in its opening note (via IGN ). "The standards and expectations regarding information security and privacy are exponentially beyond that of most employers."

The company claims that people are so hell-bent on peeking behind the curtain that it was forced to coat its building windows with a privacy film after aerial drones were used to spy on employees and photograph the inside of the building. Because of that, Rockstar has had to implement numerous security measures, such as enforcing strict no-photography rules for visitors, banning external storage devices on office premises, and restricting remote work for employees. The developer also has a full-time team of five investigators and a director who keep an eye out for potential leaks.

articles.title: Miami Approves 'Discreet' GTA 6 Marketing Campaign So the City Can Fix Its Football Field
articles.summary: Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto 6 is coming to real-life Miami after a city meeting resulted in the approval of a "discreet" – and controversial – marketing campaign.
body: The City of Miami Beach gave the OK for the famed game developer to bring GTA 6 to the area September 10, 2026, following a 4-3 vote in favor of the decision. The meeting saw strong arguments on both sides, with the deal promising that Rockstar will pay at least $3 million to the city as related logos and branding populate the town from October 15 – December 31.

GTA 6's Vice City setting is, of course, based on the very real Miami, Florida, and Rockstar is looking to capitalize on that. Arguments against the move touched on the violence of the Grand Theft Auto series, which, as stated by Commissioner David Suarez, allows players to "steal cars, deal drugs, commit robberies, murder civilians, and assassinate police officers."

articles.title: The Long Game: 4 Tactics to Master Early in Star Wars Zero Company
articles.summary: We’re back for another installment of our The Long Game series, where we focus on things you can invest in early in games that will pay off in the long run. Today we’re diving into Star Wars Zero Company, the turn-based tactics game from Bit Reactor that drops you into the twilight of the Clone…
body: Zero Company gives you lots of ways to customize your team, including a variety of specializations (aka character classes), different weapon types, weapon mods, and equippable items that can define each character’s playstyle. You can swap all of these things at the Den at any time, giving you flexibility and allowing you to experiment with different builds for characters and teams.

But regardless of what builds you use, there are some things you’ll need to get a handle on no matter what. Zero Company is a great introduction to the turn-based tactical genre, but it throws a lot at you during its tutorial missions. If you’re new to the genre, it can be tough to remember everything or realize how important some of the basics are.

That’s what we’re here to help with today. These are four things that you can utilize from the opening chapters all the way to the end of the game, and mastering them early can really help your missions run smoothly.

articles.title: EA’s New Owners May Be Considering An Even Bigger Gaming Empire
articles.summary: EA has officially been sold, and with Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund now the majority shareholder in the video game company, talks are reportedly underway to merge it with Savvy Games Group, the gaming and esports holding company that's also owned by the PIF.
body: Speaking to Bloomberg, sources said the PIF is aiming to foster "better coordination" between its gaming assets, and the merger could happen once it completes its plan to acquire Chinese mobile gaming company Moonton, a deal valued at $6 billion. The PIF also owns Pokemon Go developer Scopely and game publisher SNK, and it holds sizable stakes in video game publishers like Nintendo, Capcom, and Koei Tecmo.

The move could face scrutiny from regulators across the globe, however, as this would place several of the biggest gaming franchises in the world under one roof, including EA Sports FC, Battlefield, and mobile juggernauts like Monopoly Go. While EA's acquisition is valued at $55 billion, the massive leveraged buyout has also saddled the game company with billions of debt that needs to be addressed.

The PIF is the majority owner of EA Games, with a 93.4% stake in the company, while its partners Silver Lake and Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner's private equity firm, Affinity Partners, own 5.5% and 1.1% of the company, respectively.

articles.title: 'They Thought It Was Too Funny': Zach Cregger Says He's Cut Most of the Jokes From His Resident Evil Movie, Following Test Screenings
articles.summary: Resident Evi l director Zach Cregger says he's cut most of movie's jokes, after test audiences apparently found the film "too funny." Capcom loves including the occasional quip or witty one-liner in its Resident Evil game series — typically something cheesy from Leon S.
body: Cregger himself is known for mixing horror and dark humor to great effect, as seen in his previous projects Weapons and Barbarians. But you can also have too much of a good thing, the director has said.

"I learned that people really liked the movie, but they thought it was too funny," Cregger said of the film's test screenings, in an interview with The Hollywood Reporter. "So over the course of my testing, I stripped out as much of the jokes as possible.

"I then found that not only did the audience enjoy the movie more, but I also liked the movie a lot more," he continued. "A little bit of humor goes a long way in a horror movie, and there's not a single joke I took out of this movie that I miss."

articles.title: Switch 2 Update Secretly Makes Digital Game Sharing Much Better
articles.summary: Everyone is focused on VRR (variable refresh rate) support for Switch 2 while docked. But the latest system update just provided a notable quality-of-life improvement for people--especially families--who own multiple Switch 2 and Switch consoles.
body: For example, say your child is playing Super Mario Bros. Wonder on your old Switch OLED, but you want to play it on your Switch 2. You both can actually play the title simultaneously by turning off Wi-Fi on the original hybrid console. Then, on your Switch 2, you can utilize an online license to jump around as the mustached plumber, too. We tested this out successfully.

This also helps a lot between manually sending virtual game cards back and forth between Switch and Switch 2 systems. Now I can just start say, Blasphemous, on either system without having to actually send it from the previous place to a new one. Sure, it's not as smooth as using apps across Apple devices, but it's a step in the right direction.

Here's Nintendo's official language for the version 23.0.0 update, which incorporates Switch 2 and Switch. "When starting software, if a virtual game card cannot be ejected from another console because it is powered off or otherwise not connected to the internet, there will be a prompt to start the software using an online license."

articles.title: Death Stranding Franchise Likely Barely Broke Even, Could Explain Sony Dropping Physint – Analyst
articles.summary: With Sony no longer involved in the production of Hideo Kojima's Metal Gear Solid spiritual successor, Physint, people are wondering why the PlayStation company decided to part ways with the veteran game designer's upcoming game.
body: Why would it take another loss in the court of public opinion? Reportedly, Kojima's recent games haven't been big earners for Sony, which could be why Sony decided to cease funding for Physint.

According to a Bloomberg report, people familiar with the project have expressed concerns about Physint's development, as it has reportedly missed deadlines and could be going over budget. With Physint potentially being a timed exclusive for PlayStation, it's claimed that the company was reluctant to invest hundreds of millions of dollars in a game it would not own.

Alinea Analytics' Rhys Elliott also weighed in on the situation, saying, "From a strictly financial perspective, though, I can understand Sony's position. In a vacuum, anyway. PR and optics still matter. Ballpark math: word on the street is that the first Death Stranding cost about $100 million to make, and the second somewhere in the $150 million – $200 million ballpark (longer dev cycle, COVID, and all that). Depending on marketing overhead and the opportunity cost of pulling those Guerrilla developers onto Death Stranding, the franchise has almost certainly broken even--but not by much."

articles.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation director says Square Enix would have to compromise "the quality of the final chapter" to ship the game fully on disc
articles.summary: Physical versions of Final Fantasy 7 Revelation require a download anyway because Square Enix would've had to compromise the game in some fashion to contain the entire mammoth adventure in a disc. At least, that's the reasoning series director Naoki Hamaguchi has given.
body: Anyone sitting in the venn diagram middle of Final Fantasy 7 fan and physical games collector might have gone from extremely happy to kinda bummed earlier this week. The third and final part of the Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy is shipping in a physical format on all three major consoles (hurray), but you'll still need to download additional game data to get going.

"Each platform has limitations when it comes to physical media capacity, but we believed that compromising the quality of the final chapter in order to achieve a fully on-disc release would ultimately not be in the best interest of many fans," said Remake trilogy director Naoki Hamaguchi in an online statement.

"We understand that this decision may not meet everyone's expectations. Even so, in today's market, where the industry is steadily moving toward a disc-less future, we believe there is real value in being able to offer a physical edition at all," he added.

articles.title: Metroid Ravenous’ Surprise Reveal Was Secretly the Star of Nintendo’s Busy Week
articles.summary: It was quite the week for Nintendo. A pair of back-to-back Direct showcases gave fans a lot to talk about, even if not all the news was equally exciting. The headliner of the week, of course, was The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.
body: But that’s not the game occupying space in my brain following Nintendo’s busy week. That honor belongs to Metroid Ravenous. Samus’ new 2D adventure, which is set to lead the 2027 charge on Jan. 28, is looking like the Switch 2’s most stylish, exciting exclusive to date — at least based on a strong debut trailer that features Samus eating her enemies. We’ll only have to wait a few short months to find out if it lives up to its predecessor, the Game of the Year-nominated Metroid Dread, but it’s a good reminder that Nintendo’s current remake craze is paying off in the long-run.

The road to Metroid Ravenous started with a remake. Nintendo shocked Metroid fans back at E3 2017 when it revealed that it was remaking Metroid 2: Return of Samus as Metroid: Samus Returns, a full reimagining for the Nintendo 3DS. Even more surprising was that development on it was being led by MercurySteam. It sounded like a left-field choice, given that the team had no real connection to Nintendo, but it made perfect sense given that the studio was behind 2010’s well-received Castlevania: Lords of Shadow. Why not hand the keys to a small developer who already knew the Metroidvania genre?

articles.title: More than 40% of people cancelling Xbox Game Pass, PlayStation Plus and Nintendo Switch Online subscriptions blame rising costs
articles.summary: Players cancelling their subscriptions to video game services like Xbox Game Pass and PlayStation Plus are more likely to blame rising costs today than they were at the start of the year.
body: That's according to new data shared by Circana's senior director and video game analyst Mat Piscatella, who explained that more people are being pushed out of monthly video game subscriptions due to costs, at least, in the US.

"According to Circana's Future of Insights for Video Games Consumer Survey, cost is becoming a stronger driver of US cancellations to Xbox Game Pass Essential, PS Plus Essential and Nintendo Switch Online," Piscatella said on BlueSky. "Over 40% of those canceling in the US cite cost as a primary driver, higher than seen in Q1."

Piscatella is quick to note this data doesn't indicate that more people are cancelling video game subscriptions. "It has no relation to the number of people canceling," he wrote. It's just that the people who have given up on memberships are more likely to point the finger at costs instead of, let's say, a weak selection of games.

articles.title: How to fly helicopters in Wardogs
articles.summary: If you want to level up your pilot skill, you need to know how to fly a helicopter in Wardogs. The latest hit FPS game has a skill system that is all about actually doing actions, such as spotting enemies, healing allies, and ferrying passengers to the battlefield.
body: If you want to be able to take allies to the battlefield without crashing directly into a tree or hitting the ground too quickly, here's a quick guide on how to fly in Wardogs.

Helicopters are the only aerial vehicle in Wardogs right now and while there are a few different types available, the MH-6 is the cheapest, easiest to fly, and by far the most recommended. There's no point investing in the Z20 Lakota or Havoc until you're a master at flying safely, and you don't want to worry about the AH-6 variants with weapons because your job is to be a pilot first and foremost. Also, the MH-6 is the only one you'll even be able to buy until you've earned more pilot experience.

When it comes to actually getting that little bird in the air, Kane Allard, a senior producer on Wardogs told me at Gamescom that he recommends pilots abandon mouse and keyboard entirely. Instead, switch to a controller whenever you're piloting a chopper, because it's much easier to control. After testing out this theory, he's bang on the money.

articles.title: Star Wars' Andor Prequel Highlights Its Most Relentless Rebel in New Look
articles.summary: The beauty of Star Wars is that there’s something for everyone — whether you’re a fan of the mystical Jedi and Sith or of the spies, soldiers, and mercenaries who make up the Republic and Imperial ground forces.
body: That’s why the Reign of the Empire trilogy, which follows Mon Mothma, Bail Organa, and Saw Gerrera during the years of Imperial occupation leading up to A New Hope, feels like a breath of fresh air.

Edge of the Abyss by Rebecca Roanhorse, published by Random House Worlds, is the second book in the trilogy. Set a year before Andor, the novel follows Mon, Bail, and Saw, who have endured thirteen years of Imperial rule. After a festival attack goes awry, it sets in motion events that none of them can ignore. It also reveals something sinister: the Empire isn’t content with using violence to oppress its people but is radicalizing the new generation growing up — including Mon's and Bail’s teenage daughters, Leida and Leia.

This exclusive excerpt from Reign of the Empire: Edge of the Abyss features Saw Gerrera and Bail Organa meeting on Alderaan to talk about the tense events at Inusagi during the Blossom Festival and the people they’ve lost over the years.

articles.title: "The more aroused the fly is the harder it tries to shoot" - Google's fully mapped fly brain is now playing Doom, Beat Saber, and more
articles.summary: It's science-fiction Friday as Google's fully mapped fly brain, which was revealed last week, has been engineered to play Doom and rhythm-action game Beat Saber.
body: Google's brain-mapping is a historic first and the model of the fly brain - which took years of work and AI-help to compile - was released by the company's research team and made available for download. A few days later, as reported by PC Gamer, this resulted in the brain being trained to play Doom.

"I'm training a fly brain to play Doom using the full MaleCNS v1.0 fruit fly connectome," announced Coinbase engineer Alex Wormuth, who also published a live video feed of the simulated fly's progress. Apparently it played thousands of times and is still not doing very well.

Not long after, another enterprising engineer, domi on Bluesky, got the fly brain playing lightsaber-based rhythm-action game Beat Saber. A video shows a little fly model waving the lightsabers around and slicing through advancing tiles, probably better than I would.

The same modder got the fly brain playing shooters, using the fly's brain to work out when to turn, apparently, and its "courtship song" for when to shoot. "The more aroused the fly is the harder it tries to shoot," domi noted, alarmingly.

points: With the plethora of information and gameplay now out in the wild for Grand Theft Auto 6, it's now time to think about what it is that Rockstar still needs to show us before the launch of GTA 6.
In this week's episode of GTFM, we chat about all the gameplay mechanics, and systems that Rockstar has still yet to deliver.
We go over social media integration, side activities, how Jason and Lucia's relationship dynamic can change how and what you play, and more!
While you wait for Netflix's next GTA 6 extended look, join us we speculate what's next.

body: Marvel's Wolverine is finally here, delivering a polished, visceral single-player action experience on PS5.
